subject: [Notice] EU-West scheduled service cycle — minimal disruption expected
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: ops@cumulus.ai, platform-sre@acmehealth.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-14 09:12:00 +00:00
Subject: [Notice] EU-West scheduled service cycle — minimal disruption expected

Hi team,

Were planning a short, staged service cycle in eu-west on Wednesday 2026-10-21 between 02:00-06:00 UTC. This is a planned operational cycle that includes a targeted microcode + I/O driver alignment and a graceful service restart of select node pools. The goal is to reduce the chance of a sporadic KV cache regression we observed in a small set of long-running sessions.

What to expect
- Scope: ~12% of capacity in eu-west (non-single-tenant pools).
- Window: 02:009:00 UTC. We will operate in three 90-minute stages with short handoffs; individual customer-affecting evictions will be rare and we expect most requests to continue with sub-second latency.
- Impact: brief connection bounce for some streaming sessions (reconnect required). API request latency increases may occur for <2 minutes on affected hosts. No model or data migration is required.

Mitigations in place
- Canary first: two canary racks (10% of the stage) will validate KV warmup and latency before each stage proceeds.
- Automatic fallback: requests routed to alternative pools in-region and, if capacity is constrained, to nearest compatible variants per your routing policy.
- Observability: per-route dashboards and token-level traces will be monitored; health probes will trigger automatic rollbacks if we detect regressions.

Action items for customers
- If you have long-running streams, please plan for reconnect logic or use our streaming-resume header; we will publish best-practice snippets in the runbook.
- If you rely on pinned single-tenant capacity, there will be no change; pinned pools are out-of-scope.

Attachments: eu-west-service-cycle-runbook-v1.pdf (includes canary checklist, rollback criteria), canary-health-checks.csv

Well post live updates to https://status.redwood.ai/incident/2026-10-eu-cycle during the window. Apologies for the inconvenience — were aiming for a low-risk, fast cycle. If you want to coordinate a custom maintenance agreement or need to be excluded from the stage, reply to this thread and well arrange it.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

----
Internal notes (not in external send): canaries run at +10m, +70m, +140m; escalation policy: Marissa -> Grace -> Jordan.

From: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@acmehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: platform-sre@acmehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-14 11:05:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: [Notice] EU-West scheduled service cycle — minimal disruption expected

Thanks for the heads up, Ben. A couple quick questions from our SRE team:

1) Whats the expected behavior for streaming inference sessions that are >30 minutes long? Will tokens be re-sent after reconnect, or do clients need to replay?
2) Do you have an estimate for how many of our inference requests might be routed to other variants (we have a small set of latency-sensitive endpoints)?
3) If we see errors during your canary stage, how do we open an immediate support incident to get you to halt and roll back?

Wed like to avoid any silent throttling impacting our SLA. If possible, pls confirm whether we can be in the first stage or excluded.

Best,
Sara
Platform SRE Lead
Acme Health

On Wed, 14 Oct 2026 at 09:12, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Hi team,
> 
> Were planning a short, staged service cycle in eu-west on Wednesday 2026-10-21 between 02:00-06:00 UTC....
>

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lewis <sara.lewis@acmehealth.com>, ops@cumulus.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, jordan_blake@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-14 14:23:00 +00:00
Subject: Re: [Notice] EU-West scheduled service cycle — minimal disruption expected

Sara — great questions. Answers below and next steps.

1) Long-running streaming sessions:
- Short-lived reconnects: most streams will resume without token replay if you use our streaming-resume header. Well attach example client snippets in the runbook (and include a tiny helper lib).
- For deterministic workloads where replay is required, clients should checkpoint locally; we dont auto-replay application-level inputs.

2) Routing to other variants:
- We expect <3% of total requests from any given customer to be routed to alternative variants under normal canary progression. For your latency-sensitive endpoints we can pin routing to the primary pool for the first stage if you prefer; that will increase the stages time-on-host but reduce cross-variant routing. Let us know which endpoints (route IDs) youd like pinned.

3) Immediate support and rollback:
- If you see elevated 5xx or sustained latency beyond the rollback threshold in the canary (see canary-health-checks.csv), open an urgent ticket to support@redwood.ai with "URGENT: eu-west cycle" in the subject. Our on-call will pause the rollout and either rollback the stage or extend canary verification.

We can also schedule Acme Health in the first stage to minimize any cross-variant diversion — confirm which route IDs to pin and Ill update the canary config.

Summary of next steps Ill take:
- Publish small client examples for streaming-resume and a lightweight helper library.
- Update runbook to include a customer-exclusion process and a simple form for pinned endpoints.
- Mark Acme Health as "first-stage if requested" until 2026-10-18 16:00 UTC.

If anything changes Ill send an update; otherwise you should see the runbook live by EOD today.

Thanks,

Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: eu-west-service-cycle-runbook-v1.pdf (updated), canary-health-checks.csv

----
Internal: Marissa to coordinate canary dashboards; Grace to validate rollback play; Jordan to confirm traffic-shaping entries in the routing table.
